compare_blocks.body:
Do not read quiet as having no view. ISFP may not compete for the floor in a meeting and may have booked the right restaurant by the time it ends; ENTJ may talk a great deal and spend the whole meeting waiting for a judgement from someone he trusts. How much anyone says follows role, preparation and the state of the day, and is not a reading of preference.

Do not read volume as attitude. ENTJ may raise his voice because time is short, the room is loud, or simply out of habit; ISFP's tone dropping may mean a boundary was touched, or only that he is tired. Guessing motive from tone is the easiest way to be wrong; asking what you meant by that is more reliable.

Do not judge by lifestyle either. Dressing with care, taking photographs, cooking — none of it belongs to either type, and all of it can be shaped by experience and profession. The reverse holds: dressing plainly and never taking a photograph says nothing about which side someone leans to.

One more thing is often missed: do not take who looks like the person in charge as a type difference. Being in charge is created by authority and signature — whoever signs the confirmation letter and can change the itinerary is in charge, and that has no necessary relation to who talks more or who decides faster.

**Framework sources**: preference definitions follow the [Myers-Briggs official facts page](https://www.themyersbriggs.com/en-us/support/mbti-facts); type dynamics follows the [Foundation's note on type dynamics](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-processes/) and the [type dynamics overview](https://www.myersbriggs.org/unique-features-of-myers-briggs/type-dynamics-overview/). The Foundation provides the type-dynamics framework. The note below explains the editorial choice for the third process.

**Four-position convention on this page**: Te–Ni–Se–Fi for ENTJ and Fi–Se–Ni–Te for ISFP, particularly the attitude of the third process (Se for ENTJ, Ni for ISFP), follow the common in-site writing and are an editorial convention; sources handle it differently, and this writing is not presented as the Foundation's only reading.

**Editorial fiction note**: the reception itinerary, the six-person delegation's extra half day and the fortnight with a parent are editorial fiction, corresponding to no real delegation, institution or family, used only to practise telling grounds apart, and constituting no protocol, medical or family advice.

**Scope limits**: type descriptions are not for ranking ability, hiring screens or predicting relationships, and not for judging who is better suited to hosting or to talking with a relative; clinical judgement belongs with qualified professionals. The FermatMind assessment uses a separate item bank and scoring, set out in the [scoring and evidence notes](/en/tests/mbti-personality-test-16-personality-types#method-and-evidence).

FermatMind Editorial

- [ENTJ: base preferences led by extraverted Thinking](/en/personality/entj)
- [ISFP: base preferences led by introverted Feeling](/en/personality/isfp)
- [Browse the 16 types: compare other base descriptions](/en/personality)

A/T further reading: this is the NERIS Identity dimension from 16Personalities, covering self-evaluation, self-assurance and response to pressure, and not a fifth official MBTI dimension; A marks a steadier self-evaluation, T a greater sensitivity to pressure and self-doubt. It is scored on a different frame from the four axes and the stacks above, which is why it is listed separately.
